note: Exact reader wording for named-human review. No projection changes and no publications.

cards.public_summary: Tori McElhaney relayed Kevin Stefanski's announcement that Michael Penix Jr. was cleared for full 11-on-11 work Monday.
cards.evidence: "This is a big step for Mike, and he is excited for it," Kevin Stefanski on Michael Penix Jr. getting the green light to participate in full 11-on-11 periods in practice today.
cards.commentary: This is the next checkpoint we wanted to see. Full-team work puts Penix much closer to normal football activity, even though one practice does not settle his Week 1 workload.
cards.author: Tori McElhaney

cards.public_summary: Aaron Wilson observed Jaylin Noel getting more work in Houston's offense, including underneath routes and a touchdown catch Monday.
cards.evidence: Jaylin Noel incorporated into the Texans offense more today with a touchdown catch and some underneath routes.
cards.commentary: One practice is one practice, but this is exactly the usage we want from a slot candidate. Noel is healthy again and earning touches while Houston sorts out the targets left by Jayden Higgins.
cards.author: Aaron Wilson

cards.public_summary: Hondo Carpenter reported preliminary information pointed to an ankle sprain for Ashton Jeanty, with more testing still pending.
cards.evidence: Adam Schefter reported that Jeanty is believed to have sprained his ankle and that the injury is not considered long term. A Raiders source told Hondo Carpenter that more tests were expected before anything became definitive.
cards.commentary: The first update is far better than the scene at practice, but this remains an injury with no firm timetable. For now, Jeanty's draft price carries more short-term risk and Mike Washington matters a lot more.
cards.author: Hondo Carpenter

cards.public_summary: Alain Poupart observed Quinn Ewers back at Dolphins practice Monday for the first time since his reported groin injury.
cards.evidence: Quarterback Quinn Ewers was back at practice for the first time since the preseason opener against the Washington Commanders when he sustained what was reported as a groin injury. The non-first-team work was conducted at half speed.
cards.commentary: Getting back on the field matters, especially with roster decisions coming. For now, the half-speed setting keeps this from being a full clearance signal.
cards.author: Alain Poupart

cards.public_summary: Alain Poupart observed Chris Bell practice without a red jersey Monday for the first time since his NFI activation.
cards.evidence: Rookie wide receiver Chris Bell practiced without a red jersey for the first time since being activated from the Non-Football Injury list. Most backup team work was at half speed, though Bell received two full-speed reps.
cards.commentary: Bell shedding the red jersey is real progress. For now, the mostly half-speed practice means we should treat it as another recovery step, not proof that he is all the way back.
cards.author: Alain Poupart

cards.public_summary: Alain Poupart observed Jalen Tolbert win at the back of the end zone for a red-zone touchdown during Monday's Dolphins practice.
cards.evidence: Jalen Tolbert had a nice touchdown catch in a red zone period when he went up in the back of the end zone to beat safety Michael Taaffe.
cards.commentary: We are not turning one practice touchdown into a depth-chart declaration. It is still a useful note for a receiver trying to carve out a role in a wide-open Miami group.
cards.author: Alain Poupart

cards.public_summary: Alain Poupart observed Greg Dulcich make a difficult catch over the middle on a pass thrown behind him Monday.
cards.evidence: Tight end Greg Dulcich had a nice high catch over the middle on a Malik Willis pass thrown a bit behind him.
cards.commentary: It is only one catch, and that is fine. In a thin Miami pass-catching group, every sign that Dulcich is earning useful middle-of-field work belongs on the radar.
cards.author: Alain Poupart

cards.public_summary: Patricia Traina reported John Harbaugh said the roster standing for Tyrone Tracy Jr. remains under evaluation after two costly preseason mistakes.
cards.evidence: Tracy missed a blitz pickup in the preseason opener and lost a fumble inside Miami's 10-yard line the following week. Harbaugh said the pecking order remains to be determined over the next week.
cards.commentary: The coach is not burying Tracy, but pass protection and ball security are the two mistakes that can shrink a running back's role fast. Najee Harris and Devin Singletary make the next week especially important.
cards.author: Patricia Traina

cards.public_summary: Jay Morrison reported Erick All played nine snaps in his first game action in 657 days following a two-surgery ACL recovery.
cards.evidence: Erick All Jr. started against Chicago and played nine snaps on the opening series, his first game action in 657 days. He had needed two surgeries after learning his original college ACL repair was not done properly.
cards.commentary: Nine snaps without a target will not move a projection, but getting through live action after that recovery absolutely matters. This is a health milestone worth tracking into the final preseason week.
cards.author: Jay Morrison

cards.public_summary: Henry Cheal reported Christian McCaffrey said his camp absence was part of a planned workload ramp-down and that he feels fresh.
cards.evidence: McCaffrey said the absence was part of a plan to ramp up for nine or ten practices, come back down and then ramp up again for Week 1. He told reporters that he feels great and fresh.
cards.commentary: That explanation is much easier to live with than an unexplained hold-in or a new injury. The 49ers are managing their centerpiece, and McCaffrey says his body is responding.
cards.author: Henry Cheal

cards.public_summary: Mike Moraitis reported Joe Milton III completed 9 of 13 passes for 179 yards, two passing scores and one rushing touchdown Saturday.
cards.evidence: Milton completed 9 of 13 passes for 179 yards and two touchdowns without an interception, then added a rushing score. Through two preseason games he has completed 75 percent of his passes for 289 yards and four total touchdowns.
cards.commentary: Milton has made the Dallas QB2 race a real conversation. The athletic ceiling was never the question; two straight efficient games are evidence that the decision-making is catching up.
cards.author: Mike Moraitis

cards.public_summary: John McMullen reported Carson Steele caught six of seven targets for 84 yards and a touchdown against New England.
cards.evidence: Carson Steele caught six of seven targets for 84 yards, including a 20-yard touchdown on which he hurdled a defender. It was his second hurdle of the game.
cards.commentary: That receiving line is hard to ignore for a player fighting to stick. Steele still has to survive cutdown day, but he just gave Philadelphia a reason to keep the versatile back around.
cards.author: John McMullen

cards.public_summary: Ralph Ventre reported Ja'Mori Maclin caught two passes for 108 yards and a touchdown against Cleveland.
cards.evidence: Undrafted rookie Ja'Mori Maclin made two long receptions for 108 yards and one touchdown against Cleveland, including a 71-yard score. Joe Brady said Maclin showed enough early to remain in Buffalo's plans.
cards.commentary: Maclin is no longer just a camp name. He has at least pushed his way into the practice-squad picture and made Buffalo's final receiver decision more interesting.
cards.author: Ralph Ventre

cards.public_summary: Brendon Nelson relayed Gregg Bell's report that Seattle plans to sit Jadarian Price in every preseason game.
cards.evidence: Gregg Bell reported that Jadarian Price would not play in either of Seattle's final two preseason games. The article said the decision was about protecting the expected starter rather than a current injury.
cards.commentary: Seattle treating Price like a player it cannot afford to lose says plenty about his September role. The rookie will enter Week 1 without exhibition reps, so the workload is exciting but not risk-free.
cards.author: Brendon Nelson

cards.public_summary: Fantasy On SI argues Malik Nabers is a draft value after he progressed to team-controlled drills in a red non-contact jersey.
cards.evidence: Nabers progressed from individual work to team-controlled drills while wearing a red non-contact jersey. The article notes that he is being drafted around WR12-WR13 and argues he has top-10 upside if healthy.
cards.commentary: The injury discount is starting to look more interesting than scary. Nabers still needs contact clearance, but team work puts his WR12-WR13 price squarely in the upside zone.
cards.author: Gray Deyo

cards.public_summary: Fantasy On SI argues George Kittle is undervalued at a TE10-TE11 ADP after his PUP activation and recent recovery report.
cards.evidence: The article relays that Kittle was ahead of schedule after a medical visit and that San Francisco activated him from PUP. It cites a TE10 ADP on Sleeper and TE11 on ESPN.
cards.commentary: TE10 pricing leaves room for a few missed games and still gives us access to elite per-game production. Kittle is one of the clearest injury-discount swings on the board right now.
cards.author: Gray Deyo

cards.public_summary: The article argues Mike Washington can handle early-down RB1 work if Ashton Jeanty misses time, while noting third downs remain unsettled.
cards.evidence: Jared Feinberg wrote that Washington's power, downhill speed, contact balance and improved vision fit the Raiders' system. He noted that Dylan Laube would be the more likely third-down option.
cards.commentary: Washington is no longer a generic handcuff. The early-down case is strong enough to draft, but the passing-game caveat keeps us from treating him like a full three-down replacement.
cards.author: Jared Feinberg

cards.public_summary: The article argues Malik Davis deserves Dallas's RB2 role after an efficient preseason showing and useful pass-protection work.
cards.evidence: Davis ran five times for 29 yards, caught an eight-yard touchdown and picked up a blitz in pass protection against Arizona. The article contrasts his consistency with Jaydon Blue's ball-security issues.
cards.commentary: This is exactly the kind of boring depth-chart fight that produces useful late-round value. Davis is making the trust plays coaches notice, even if Blue remains the more explosive name.
cards.author: Josh Sanchez

cards.public_summary: Fantasy On SI argues Chuba Hubbard remains the better value at RB29 than the rapidly rising Jonathon Brooks.
cards.evidence: The analysis projects Hubbard for 50 percent of Carolina's rushing work and Brooks for 31 percent. It ranks Hubbard RB22 against a consensus RB29 ADP and says his hamstring tweak should not keep him from Week 1.
cards.commentary: Hubbard is the less exciting click, which is exactly why the price works. Pass protection and a Week 1 lead role give him a much cleaner path to paying off than the market is admitting.
cards.author: Thomas Carelli

cards.public_summary: Fantasy On SI argues Jonathon Brooks has climbed above fair value because his role and post-injury workload remain uncertain.
cards.evidence: The article says Brooks has started both preseason games but projects him for 31 percent of Carolina's rushing work. It calls his RB33 consensus ADP too aggressive for a back returning from a major injury.
cards.commentary: The talent case is easy to understand; the price is the problem. Brooks now asks us to pay for a takeover before we know his workload, and Hubbard is still built to hold the important snaps.
cards.author: Thomas Carelli

cards.public_summary: Fantasy On SI prefers Rashee Rice for ceiling over DeVonta Smith when managers are comfortable accepting more availability risk.
cards.evidence: The analysis views Rice as the higher-risk, higher-reward choice because of his yards-after-catch skill, red-zone role and Patrick Mahomes connection. It identifies availability as the main concern.
cards.commentary: Rice is the aggressive pick in this range. If the roster can absorb volatility, the path to WR1 weeks is more exciting than the safer alternatives around him.
cards.author: Daniel Outerbridge

cards.public_summary: Fantasy On SI identifies DeVonta Smith as the safer pick over Rashee Rice because of his established production and weekly floor.
cards.evidence: The article calls Smith the safer WR2 and points to his route running, established production and expanded role after A.J. Brown's departure. It notes that added defensive attention is the primary risk.
cards.commentary: Smith is the clean roster-construction pick. He may not match Rice's spike-week ceiling, but the new alpha role gives us a reliable way to bank targets without taking on the same availability risk.
cards.author: Daniel Outerbridge

cards.public_summary: Fantasy On SI prefers Tee Higgins over Emeka Egbuka because Higgins carries less health risk in a stronger passing offense.
cards.evidence: The analysis ranks Higgins WR17 and projects a 23 percent share of Cincinnati's passing offense. It prefers his floor and top-10 upside over Egbuka while the Tampa Bay receiver manages turf toe.
cards.commentary: Higgins does not need Ja'Marr Chase to disappear to pay off. Joe Burrow and a huge passing pie keep the weekly ceiling high enough to justify taking the steadier side of this debate.
cards.author: Thomas Carelli

cards.public_summary: Fantasy On SI argues Emeka Egbuka's WR19 ADP carries added risk while he works back from turf toe.
cards.evidence: The analysis says Egbuka is dealing with turf toe and may not be 100 percent for Week 1. It ranks him WR26 against a WR19 ADP while acknowledging the top-10 ceiling he showed before last year's hamstring injury.
cards.commentary: Egbuka can absolutely beat this take, but WR19 leaves very little room for a slow start. We would rather buy the ceiling after the toe risk is reflected in the price.
cards.author: Thomas Carelli

cards.public_summary: Fantasy On SI highlights Terrance Ferguson as a deep sleeper at TE26 because he has a path to the Rams' third receiving role.
cards.evidence: The article lists Ferguson at a 194.7 consensus ADP and argues he is effectively the Rams' third receiver behind Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. It also notes Sean McVay's praise for the second-year tight end.
cards.commentary: TE26 is the perfect price for this bet. Ferguson does not need a huge weekly role to matter, and one injury ahead of him would put a Sean McVay target funnel in play.
cards.author: Skyler Carlin

cards.public_summary: Fantasy On SI highlights Ray Davis as a late handcuff with standalone touches and a larger path while Ty Johnson is sidelined.
cards.evidence: The analysis lists Davis at RB64 and notes that James Cook has never reached a 56 percent offensive snap rate. It points to Ty Johnson's knee injury and Davis's 13.8 percent explosive-run rate.
cards.commentary: Davis gives us two ways to win: a few useful touches now and a much bigger role if Cook misses time. That is exactly what we want after pick 200.
cards.author: Skyler Carlin

cards.public_summary: Fantasy On SI highlights Pat Bryant as a WR82 deep sleeper with a path to steady three-receiver work in Denver.
cards.evidence: The article lists Bryant at WR82 and notes that he earned at least five targets in four of his final six rookie-season games. It argues his build fits an every-down role better than Denver's gadget options.
cards.commentary: Bryant is free, and the route to snaps is believable. We are not drafting a guaranteed starter; we are drafting a big receiver who can stay on the field if the veterans miss time.
cards.author: Skyler Carlin

cards.public_summary: The article identifies Daniel Jones as a QB24 value after a full camp and a top-five fantasy start to the 2025 season.
cards.evidence: The Colts analysis says Jones is going around QB24 after ranking QB5 through the first ten weeks of 2025. It notes that he has been full-go in camp following his Achilles injury.
cards.commentary: QB24 is a cheap way to buy rushing points in a Shane Steichen offense. The Achilles history is real, but the camp participation makes Jones one of the better late quarterback swings.
cards.author: Michael Greene

cards.public_summary: The article identifies Josh Downs as its favorite Colts value at a WR42 PPR price entering a contract season.
cards.evidence: The analysis calls Downs its favorite value in the Colts offense and cites a WR42 PPR ADP after a 58-catch, 566-yard season. It notes that Downs expects more opportunity this year.
cards.commentary: WR42 is a friendly price for a slot receiver with something to prove and a quarterback who will use the middle of the field. Downs is the Colts receiver we want first at cost.
cards.author: Michael Greene

cards.public_summary: The article identifies Alec Pierce as a late-round upside play if his current injury pushes his draft price down.
cards.evidence: The Colts analysis notes that Pierce topped 1,000 yards with six touchdowns and led the league at 21.3 yards per catch last season. It argues that his injury can create a useful draft discount.
cards.commentary: Pierce is the kind of player we want to buy after the room gets nervous. The weekly floor will always bounce around, but very few late picks can create this much yardage on a handful of targets.
cards.author: Michael Greene

cards.public_summary: Fantasy On SI lists Isaiah Likely as a TE13 value with a starting role and a path to become the Giants' second target.
cards.evidence: The article lists Likely at TE13 with a 125 ADP and argues his move to New York gives him a first opportunity to lead a tight end room. It says he has impressed in camp behind Malik Nabers.
cards.commentary: Likely finally has the route volume fantasy players have been waiting for. TE13 is still cheap for a player with a believable path to finishing second on his team in targets.
cards.author: Jeff Salcedo

cards.public_summary: Fantasy On SI lists Travis Kelce as a TE11 value after three straight PPR finishes inside the top five at the position.
cards.evidence: The article lists Kelce at TE11 with a 122 ADP and notes PPR finishes of TE3, TE5 and TE3 over the past three seasons. It argues the age discount has become larger than the production decline.
cards.commentary: Kelce no longer needs to be the TE1 to smash this price. At TE11, we are paying for ordinary production and getting three years of elite positional results as the upside case.
cards.author: Jeff Salcedo

cards.public_summary: Fantasy On SI lists Colston Loveland as a TE3 value because his role carries fewer questions than nearby skill-position picks.
cards.evidence: The article lists Loveland at TE3 with a 45 ADP and calls him an ascending sophomore coming off a season as Chicago's leading pass catcher. It prefers his certainty to the injury questions around nearby picks.
cards.commentary: Loveland is expensive for a tight end, but the role is unusually clean for this part of the draft. Buying the young focal point can be smarter than forcing a shakier running back or receiver.
cards.author: Jeff Salcedo

cards.public_summary: Fantasy On SI lists Harold Fannin Jr. as a TE7 value after he led Cleveland with 731 receiving yards as a rookie.
cards.evidence: The article lists Fannin at TE7 with an 86 ADP after he led the Browns with 731 receiving yards in his rookie season. It argues added receiver talent can create more one-on-one matchups.
cards.commentary: Fannin already proved he can command volume in an ugly offense. TE7 is not a giveaway, but the route and target case is much sturdier than the price suggests.
cards.author: Jeff Salcedo

cards.public_summary: Fantasy On SI identifies Dak Prescott as the safer middle-round quarterback because of Dallas's stable, pass-heavy offense.
cards.evidence: The analysis cites Prescott's 4,300-plus passing yards, 31 touchdowns and QB6 finish in 2025. It describes his passing volume as stable while noting that limited rushing narrows his path to a top-five finish.
cards.commentary: Dak is the floor play. He will not rescue a quiet passing day with his legs, but Dallas gives him enough volume to keep an otherwise aggressive roster stable at quarterback.
cards.author: Daniel Outerbridge

cards.public_summary: Fantasy On SI prefers Trevor Lawrence over Dak Prescott for his rushing floor and top-five ceiling at a lower draft cost.
cards.evidence: The analysis notes that Lawrence added nearly 400 rushing yards and five rushing touchdowns in 2025 after throwing 29 scores. It prefers his multi-dimensional ceiling at a one-round discount to Prescott.
cards.commentary: Lawrence is the better swing when we want ceiling without paying the elite-quarterback tax. The rushing work gives him more ways to win a week and more protection when the passing line is ordinary.
cards.author: Daniel Outerbridge

approval_statement: Ralph approved all 36 cards as written.
